project_summary: Implementation of Google OAuth login functionality to unblock enterprise user onboarding, creation of a secure token-based password reset flow compatible with mobile web views, and establishment of secure HttpOnly JWT session cookies with 7-day inactivity expiration.
identified_risks: Mobile web views may handle HttpOnly cookies inconsistently across OS versions.
Password reset tokens need strict short-lived expiration and single-use enforcement to prevent replay attacks.
Google OAuth account linking edge cases when existing email/password accounts share the same email address.

user_stories.title: Google OAuth Single Sign-On
user_stories.user_story: As an enterprise user, I want to sign in using my Google account, so that I can quickly and securely access the platform without maintaining another password.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user on the login page, When they click 'Sign in with Google', Then they are redirected to Google OAuth authorization prompt.
Given successful Google authorization, When the backend receives the authorization code, Then a user account is authenticated/created and a secure session is initiated.
Given an unauthenticated or canceled Google login attempt, When the user returns, Then an appropriate error message is displayed.

user_stories.title: Token-Based Password Reset Flow
user_stories.user_story: As a user on mobile web, I want to receive a secure password reset link via email, so that I can reset my forgotten password successfully without layout or session bugs.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user requests a password reset, When they submit their registered email address, Then a secure, time-limited token link is emailed to them.
Given a user clicks the reset link in a mobile web view, When they enter and submit a valid new password, Then their password is updated and the reset token is invalidated.
Given an expired or previously used token link, When accessed, Then the system informs the user that the link is invalid.

user_stories.title: Secure HttpOnly JWT Cookie & 7-Day Inactivity Expiration
user_stories.user_story: As a security administrator, I want JWTs stored in HttpOnly cookies with a 7-day inactivity expiration, so that user sessions are protected against XSS and stale sessions are automatically invalidated.
acceptance_criteria: Given a successfully authenticated user, When the session response is generated, Then the JWT is delivered via a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie.
Given an active user session, When the user performs an action within 7 days, Then the 7-day inactivity timer resets.
Given an inactive user session, When 7 consecutive days pass without user activity, Then the cookie/session expires and subsequent requests require re-authentication.
